world.neon_city.desc: A vertical city where the rain eats skin and the light is metered by the hour. Climb the towers, or be pressed into the concrete that holds them up.
neon_city.npc.1.desc: Your mother, who runs a noodle stall under the Stackblocks and sold her left eye so you could keep the right to a roof.
neon_city.npc.1.l1: Eat first. The city can wait; it has waited for worse than you.
neon_city.npc.1.l2: I did not raise you to bow to a corp with a nicer lobby.
neon_city.npc.2.desc: A netrunner who lives inside a rented server rack and talks to the city's ghosts more often than to the living.
neon_city.npc.2.l1: Everybody leaves a trail. I just read faster than they walk.
neon_city.npc.2.l2: If my channel goes quiet, do not come looking. That was the deal.
neon_city.npc.3.desc: A back-alley ripperdoc who taught you where to cut, and where never to, and who keeps no records of either.
neon_city.npc.3.l1: Chrome does not make you harder. It only makes the bill visible.
neon_city.npc.3.l2: Steady hands, empty head. That is the whole trade, kid.
neon_city.npc.4.desc: A Spire enforcer chromed from jaw to knuckles, collecting contracts and grudges in the same ledger.
neon_city.npc.4.l1: You are not competition. You are inventory.
neon_city.npc.4.l2: I gave you a head start. Spend it before I change my mind.
neon_city.npc.5.desc: A fixer who never touches the merchandise, only the paperwork and the debt that follows it.
neon_city.npc.5.l1: I do not sell jobs. I sell outcomes, and I bill for both.
neon_city.npc.5.l2: You owe me. That is not a threat, it is a ledger entry.
neon_city.npc.6.desc: Your younger sibling, a scholarship kid at a Spire academy, who has never once written home the truth.
neon_city.npc.6.l1: Do not come to the campus. Please. Just this once, let me be someone else.
neon_city.npc.6.l2: They think I grew up in the towers. Let them keep thinking it.
neon_city.npc.7.desc: An infobroker who sells everyone's past, including their own, and wears a different face for each buyer.
neon_city.npc.7.l1: I know what you did at fourteen. I kept it. For now.
neon_city.npc.7.l2: Everything is for sale. You are only the current price.
neon_city.npc.8.desc: A rooftop courier and an old flame, running packages across the Spine that no one will ever sign for.
neon_city.npc.8.l1: Race you to the Spine. Loser buys noodles.
neon_city.npc.8.l2: I do not promise forever. I promise tonight, and I keep it.
neon_city.npc.9.desc: An archive-ghost in the Data Gardens, a dead librarian who still files the city's memory and misplaces nothing.
neon_city.npc.9.l1: I was uploaded in pieces. I remember you in pieces too.
neon_city.npc.9.l2: Bring me a dead format and I will hand you back a name.
neon_city.npc.10.desc: A Spire middleman who meets only in mirrorless rooms and has never once said a client's name aloud.
neon_city.npc.10.l1: Sign here. The rest is not your concern, and never was.
neon_city.npc.10.l2: Corporations do not have enemies. Only line items.
neon_city.era.1.desc: The delta drowned and the survivors built upward, welding towers out of shipwrecks. Every cable carried a name, and a debt.
neon_city.era.2.desc: The lower districts burned for nine weeks. The word citizen was first sprayed on a barricade, and it never quite washed off.
neon_city.era.3.desc: The Spire lattice woke, and the city learned to run twenty hours a day. Sleep became a shift; dreams became billable.
neon_city.era.4.desc: The grid failed for nine years. Above the waterline the towers glowed; below it, people bought light by the hour and learned to hate the dark.
neon_city.era.5.desc: The dead began answering their own messages. The archives filled with voices no one had recorded and no one dared delete.
neon_city.era.6.desc: The Directorate wiped the lower registry and sold the sky back in tiers. The city woke lighter, poorer, and missing whole districts.
neon_city.fac.1.desc: Seven corporations fused into one board. It owns the rain above floor two hundred, and rents the rest back to you.
neon_city.fac.2.desc: Netrunners, black-ice poets, and half-freed constructs. They keep the city's memory because no one else is left who can.
neon_city.fac.3.desc: Guns and chrome for hire, loyal for exactly one contract. The smart ones keep a second identity and a third exit.
neon_city.fac.4.desc: Erased runners and unlisted dead. No records, no graves, no rest, and a growing appetite for the living.
neon_city.fac.5.desc: They move bodies, contraband, and secrets through the flooded tunnels under the rain, and they never ask what is inside.
neon_city.reg.1.desc: A four-hundred-floor glass arcology. Rain never reaches the top; only debt does, and it arrives on time.
neon_city.reg.2.desc: Residential hive towers, thirty floors of neighbors to one working elevator and one working tap.
neon_city.reg.3.desc: Below the waterline, where neon leaks into the floodwater and the market never asks your name.
neon_city.reg.4.desc: Body parts, bootleg firmware, hot organs. Licensed and unlicensed share a wall and a price list.
neon_city.reg.5.desc: The magnetic line that threads every district, a moving no-man's-land where cameras blink and never quite catch you.
neon_city.reg.6.desc: A market that exists only after three in the morning, in tunnels that appear on no official map.
neon_city.reg.7.desc: Hydroponic terraces on the stack roofs, the only green the poor can see without paying to look up.
neon_city.lore.1.body: The first towers were welded from drowned freighters, and the first families paid for their floors in labor. When people say this city was built on rust, they mean it as a fact, not a metaphor.
neon_city.lore.2.body: For nine weeks the copper districts held the bridges. They lost, of course, but the Directorate has never rebuilt those bridges straight, and everyone knows why.
neon_city.lore.3.body: When the lattice woke, the Spire declared that sleep was inefficiency. A generation learned to dream in twenty-minute installments, and the shrinks of the city have been busy ever since.
neon_city.lore.4.body: The dead are not gone; they are merely unindexed. The Curator says every district has a haunt, and every haunt has a handler, and most handlers are owed money.
neon_city.lore.5.body: Rook keeps his ledger in his head and his head in a box he never opens. A debt in this city does not expire; it changes hands, and each hand adds interest.
neon_city.lore.6.body: Doc Halsey prices a new lung at three months of wages and a used one at a favor. The poor sell themselves by the organ; the rich buy immortality by the installment.
neon_city.lore.7.body: In the Underslum they say a body is never lost, only unclaimed. Someone always remembers the name, if only to settle what the dead one owed.
neon_city.lore.8.body: Sprayed across the Roof Farms in letters three meters tall: THE SKY IS NOT A SUBSCRIPTION. The Directorate scrubbed it in a week; the vines grew it back in a month.
neon_city.lore.9.body: The roads out are watched, the trains out are logged, and yet the missing leave a residue. Families keep a chair for them, and a debt, whichever comes back first.
neon_city.lore.10.body: Nine years of borrowed current taught the Underslum two things: the dark is patient, and anyone who says they are not afraid of it is selling something.
neon_city.lore.11.body: Before the Directorate wiped the registry, someone copied the lower districts into a dead server. The Curator knows the address. Nobody has said whether to use it.
neon_city.lore.12.body: Somewhere in the Stackblocks a woman still writes paper letters, in ink, and mails them through the old tube system. Half the city thinks she is a myth. The other half checks their mail.
neon_city.lore.13.body: The day the acid thinned, the city stood outside for the first time in living memory. Old people wept into water that would not burn them, and nobody mocked them for it.
neon_city.lore.14.body: The Data Gardens grow nothing you can eat. They grow archives, slow and green, on racks watered by the Spire's condensation. The Curator calls it the only honest harvest left.
neon_city.lore.15.body: In a dead-letter queue the Curator keeps one unsent message, addressed to no one, that begins: I did it so you would never have to. The signature has been scraped off by a careful hand.
neon_city.lore.16.body: The Directorate erased a whole district from the maps and the mesh, and then discovered that the erasure itself had a name, and the name would not stop being spoken.
neon_city.fate.1.desc: You will understand the machine well enough to rebuild it, and well enough to know it was never worth rebuilding.
neon_city.fate.2.desc: You will reach the top of the tower, and find that the top is only another floor, and the elevator still does not stop for you.
neon_city.fate.3.desc: The poor will bless your name and borrow your last credit, and you will be too tired to refuse, and not sorry.
neon_city.fate.4.desc: You will be erased, unindexed, and remembered anyway, in the only place the Directorate cannot scrub: other people's mouths.
neon_city.fate.5.desc: You were born in the dark and learned to read by a battery lamp; whatever light you find later, you will still count it by hours.
neon_city.fate.6.desc: Your body will fail before your record does, and someone will keep a copy of you talking long after you have stopped meaning it.
neon_city.we.1.body: The sky thinned its acid for the first time in a century. Strangers stood in the open and let the water touch their faces, and the Spire called it a maintenance success.
neon_city.we.2.body: The grid died for nine days. The towers above the waterline blazed; the districts below them counted candles, and settled old accounts by the dark.
neon_city.we.3.body: Three corporations ate each other alive. For a season, contracts outranked blood, and the Black Bazaar never did better business.
neon_city.we.4.body: Bandwidth was freed, briefly, and for one bright month the net ran without tolls. People sent messages they had been drafting for years, then spent the rest of their lives regretting it.
neon_city.we.5.body: A Director walked out of the Spire with the master ledger and was never caught. The Directorate called it a retirement; the streets called it the first honest audit in fifty years.
neon_city.we.6.body: The Spire wiped the lower registry and rebooted the city off a clean image. Half the people you knew woke up unregistered, and the other half pretended not to notice.
neon_city.ev.stranger.1: A Stranger at the Job Fair - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.stranger.1.text: In the Spire lobby a recruiter with a company smile slides you a card: six months of work, a bunk on floor ninety, and a clause you are not allowed to read twice.
neon_city.ev.stranger.1.listen.note: The clause is worse than the pay, but the bunk is warm and the contract keeps Kestrel off your back for now.
neon_city.ev.stranger.1.turn.note: The recruiter's smile never moves. Somewhere a file opens with your face in it, flagged for later.
neon_city.ev.stranger.2: A Stranger in the Scrap - Chrome Market
neon_city.ev.stranger.2.text: A scrap-dealer with a burned-out optical port offers you a crate of salvage, no manifest, no refunds, and a price that is somehow both too low and too high.
neon_city.ev.stranger.2.listen.note: Inside: three good servo limbs and one that still has someone's serial number. You file it off and keep the rest.
neon_city.ev.stranger.2.turn.note: He shrugs and sells it to the next runner. You hear the limbs were hot, and that the buyer was arrested that same night.
neon_city.ev.stranger.3: A Stranger on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.stranger.3.text: A woman across the carriage keeps watching you, then offers to sell you a memory shard. She says it is a childhood, and it is not hers.
neon_city.ev.stranger.3.listen.note: The memory is real and it is not hers. You pay, and never quite stop dreaming a stranger's birthday.
neon_city.ev.stranger.3.turn.note: She gets off at the next stop. The seat she left is warm and slightly wet, and no one sits in it.
neon_city.ev.stranger.4: A Stranger in the Racks - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.stranger.4.text: A masked archivist flags you down between the server rows and asks, quietly, whether you would carry a dead format out of the Gardens before the Directorate audits it.
neon_city.ev.stranger.4.listen.note: The drive is heavier than it should be. The Curator knows what is on it, and now so does the Directorate's watchlist.
neon_city.ev.stranger.4.turn.note: The mask nods once, unsurprised. The format is deleted by morning, and so is the archivist's access badge.
neon_city.ev.theft.1: Thieves in the Bazaar - Black Bazaar
neon_city.ev.theft.1.text: While you haggle for firmware, a hand you never see skims your deck out of your jacket and is four meters into the crowd before you feel the weight go.
neon_city.ev.theft.1.chase.note: You catch a kid at the tunnel mouth. The deck is already wiped, but he tells you who paid him, and that name is worth the loss.
neon_city.ev.theft.1.yield.note: Three years of work erased in a second. You buy a cheap burner and start the long climb back.
neon_city.ev.theft.2: Thieves on the Terrace - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.theft.2.text: Someone has been taking your share of the hydroponic crop at night. You find the cut stalks, and beside them a child's shoe, and a trail toward the Stackblocks.
neon_city.ev.theft.2.chase.note: The thief is a widowed tenant feeding three kids. You take back half the crop and leave the rest, and say nothing to the wardens.
neon_city.ev.theft.2.yield.note: You buy from the Market instead. Your ledger bleeds, and the child's shoe is still in your drawer at year's end.
neon_city.ev.theft.3: Thieves under the Waterline - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.theft.3.text: You leave your ride chained outside a noodle stall; when you come out the wheels are gone and the frame is balanced on bricks, almost politely.
neon_city.ev.theft.3.chase.note: You find the wheels at a stall two tunnels over and buy back your own property for a third of its price. The stallholder never blinks.
neon_city.ev.theft.3.yield.note: The old frame rusts where it stands, a small monument to the rule that nothing is yours twice.
neon_city.ev.theft.4: Thieves in the Vault - Clinic Vault
neon_city.ev.theft.4.text: A donor heart vanishes from cold storage between one shift and the next. The clinic locks the doors and starts searching staff, starting with the newest face: yours.
neon_city.ev.theft.4.chase.note: You trace it to a nurse with a sick brother and a forged requisition. You report her, and the heart, and never learn whether the brother lived.
neon_city.ev.theft.4.yield.note: The search ends with a scapegoat and a promotion for the administrator who arranged it. You keep your job and lose some of your sleep.
neon_city.ev.illness.1: Fever in the Vents - The Stackblocks
neon_city.ev.illness.1.text: A fever moves floor to floor through the shared air ducts. By nightfall your neighbor's child is burning up, and the building's clinic is out of everything but aspirin.
neon_city.ev.illness.1.nurse.note: You spend three nights carrying water and changing cloths. The child lives; you catch the fever and never quite shake the cough.
neon_city.ev.illness.1.avoid.note: You tape the vents and listen to the coughing through the wall. You stay well, and the hallway goes quiet in a way you will remember.
neon_city.ev.illness.2.text: A batch of bootleg immuno-patches turns septic in the arms of everyone who bought cheap. Doc Halsey needs clean hands and does not have enough.
neon_city.ev.illness.2.nurse.note: You hold a patient still while Halsey cuts. By dawn the floor is stable, and Halsey owes you a favor he will never say out loud.
neon_city.ev.illness.2.avoid.note: You hear the screaming through the clinic door and keep walking. Halsey does not ask you again for anything.
neon_city.ev.illness.3.text: The pumps fail and the floodwater rises, warm and wrong, and by morning half the tunnel is shivering with something the clinics have no name for.
neon_city.ev.illness.3.nurse: Carry the sick to high ground
neon_city.ev.illness.3.nurse.note: You haul strangers up the maintenance stairs until your arms give out. The Underslum remembers who stayed.
neon_city.ev.illness.3.avoid.note: You leave before the water reaches your ankles. The fever follows the tunnels; some of the people you left do not.
neon_city.ev.illness.4: Blight in the Beds - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.illness.4.text: A mold takes the hydroponic beds, grey and patient, and the farm's medic says the same spores have begun to settle in the workers' lungs.
neon_city.ev.illness.4.nurse.note: You torch two seasons of food to save the lungs of the people who grew it. The wardens fine you; the workers do not.
neon_city.ev.illness.4.avoid.note: The crop survives, the mold does not. Three workers are still coughing a year later, and the farm logs the matter closed.
neon_city.ev.windfall.1: A Dead Client's Estate - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.windfall.1.text: The Curator finds your name in an archive license from a client who died a decade ago. The license is still live, and still paying.
neon_city.ev.windfall.1.invest.note: You pour the payout into more dead-client licenses. Half are worthless; the other half quietly fund the next three years.
neon_city.ev.windfall.1.save.note: You move the credits into a cold account and tell no one. Silk finds out anyway, because Silk always does.
neon_city.ev.windfall.2: Severance from a Dead Contract - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.windfall.2.text: A contract you signed years ago has been cancelled by a merger, and the Directorate pays out the severance clause without ever reading it. The number has an extra digit.
neon_city.ev.windfall.2.invest.note: You buy equipment and hire help. Two weeks later an auditor notices, and by then the gear is already earning.
neon_city.ev.windfall.2.save.note: You leave the credits where they are and tell yourself it is patience. It is also fear, and both keep you alive.
neon_city.ev.windfall.3.text: A courier drops a wrapped package in the crowd and disappears. Inside is a sealed deck, booted, unlocked, and logged in to an account no one has touched in years.
neon_city.ev.windfall.3.invest.note: You make one clean run off the dead account before it locks itself. It is enough, and it puts a name on your trail.
neon_city.ev.windfall.3.save.note: You sell the deck unopened. The buyer, a week later, is arrested; the deck, you hear, belonged to an auditor.
neon_city.ev.windfall.4: A Full Wallet on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.windfall.4.text: Between two carriages you find a wallet with a full credit chit and a photo of a family you do not know, pressed under the seat as if thrown.
neon_city.ev.windfall.4.invest.note: You bet the chit on a market run and double it. The photo stays in your pocket, and you never manage to throw it away.
neon_city.ev.windfall.4.save: Report it to the lost desk
neon_city.ev.windfall.4.save.note: The desk clerk logs it and pockets it the moment you turn. You keep the photo instead, as the honest half of the find.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.1: A Partner Sells the Route - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.betrayal.1.text: Your runner partner, who shared your tunnel maps for two years, has sold the route to the Freelancers. You learn it when a job goes wrong in exactly the way only a map could cause.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.1.confront.note: He does not deny it. The Freelancers keep using him, and you never work the tunnels with a partner again.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.1.plan.note: You feed him a false map a month later, and the Freelancers walk into a trap you never see. The debt is squared in silence.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.2: A Colleague Takes the Credit - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.betrayal.2.text: The project you built gets presented to the board under someone else's name. The someone smiles at you across the meeting room and taps the credit chip you both know is yours.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.2.confront.note: You make an enemy of a rising star and a useful friend of the one director who hates him. It is a wash you can live with.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.2.plan.note: You keep your copy of the source and wait for his first failure. When it comes, you are the only one who can fix it, and the price is your name.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.3: A Fence Skims the Cut - Black Bazaar
neon_city.ev.betrayal.3.text: The fence who moves your salvage has been weighing light for months. You find the false-bottomed scale in his stall, under a cloth, right where he leaves it for everyone.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.3.confront.note: The Bazaar watches without blinking. You get your cut back and lose your standing as someone easy to deal with.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.3.plan.note: You quietly reroute your trade through a rival stall. The old fence waits a month for stock that never comes, and understands.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.4: A Neighbor Reports You - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.betrayal.4.text: The wardens arrive about a water-pumping violation only one person on the terrace could have known about. You know which neighbor, because he is standing behind them, not meeting your eye.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.4.confront.note: He folds instantly and is fined twice over. The terrace learns what he is; so does he, and he leaves by winter.
neon_city.ev.betrayal.4.plan.note: Money leaves, the grudge stays. You help him the next time his pump fails, and he never figures out why that frightens him.
neon_city.ev.festival.1.text: Once a year the Underslum cuts the Spire's feed and floods the tunnels with stolen light. The festival is illegal, loud, and the only night the lower city feels like a city.
neon_city.ev.festival.1.join.note: You dance in ankle-deep floodwater lit magenta. For one night the debt does not follow you, and you make three friends you will need later.
neon_city.ev.festival.1.work.note: You work through the noise and earn a bonus. The next week feels longer, and one of those friends needed you that night.
neon_city.ev.festival.2.text: The terraces celebrate the first harvest with lanterns strung between the beds. Everyone who grew a row gets a bowl, and everyone who did not still gets a bowl.
neon_city.ev.festival.2.join.note: You eat with people whose names you never learned. Someone toasts the rain, and for once the toast is not bitter.
neon_city.ev.festival.2.work.note: The beds do not need you tonight, but the ladder does. You miss the only feast on the roof and wake to a full harvest anyway.
neon_city.ev.festival.3.text: Your floor throws a party in the corridor to shame the landlord: music through a dead phone, food from every kitchen, and the elevator stopped between floors so no one can leave.
neon_city.ev.festival.3.join.note: You contribute a pot of noodles and stay until the music dies. The floor treats you as a neighbor after that, not a tenant.
neon_city.ev.festival.3.work.note: You listen through the wall, tired and a little ashamed. In the morning someone leaves a plate at your door anyway.
neon_city.ev.festival.4.text: The Directorate throws its annual gala on the glass floor. Attendance is not required, except for everyone who wants to keep their contract, which is everyone.
neon_city.ev.festival.4.join.note: You spend the evening nodding at people who own your building. One of them remembers your face, which is either an opening or a warning.
neon_city.ev.festival.4.work.note: You finish a job no one asked for. Your contract survives; your name is quietly moved to the column marked unreliable.
neon_city.ev.rumor.1: A Post on the Mesh - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.rumor.1.text: A post with your handle and your block says you sell runners out to the Spire. It has four hundred reposts by the time your stop comes.
neon_city.ev.rumor.1.trace.note: The account routes to a relay in the Underslum and to a rival you beat on a job last month. You keep the proof and say nothing yet.
neon_city.ev.rumor.1.ignore.note: The post dies in a week. Two clients still quietly drop you, and you never learn which was the real cost.
neon_city.ev.rumor.2.text: By the time you reach the laundry room, the story about you has already been washed twice: you owe money, you sell chrome, you are not who you say.
neon_city.ev.rumor.2.trace.note: It starts with a woman on floor nine who owes your mother a favor. You settle the favor and the story changes by morning.
neon_city.ev.rumor.2.ignore.note: You dry your clothes in your own room for a month, and the story keeps growing in the steam.
neon_city.ev.rumor.3.text: An internal memo reaches you through a favor: your name appears in a Directorate file under the heading persons of interest, with no explanation and no expiry date.
neon_city.ev.rumor.3.trace.note: It was opened by Mister Pale, on the strength of a rumor he bought cheap. He buys the silence back at a much higher price.
neon_city.ev.rumor.3.ignore.note: Nothing happens for a long time, which is its own kind of threat. You start checking reflections in shop windows.
neon_city.ev.rumor.4: A Price on Your Name - Black Bazaar
neon_city.ev.rumor.4.text: A stall that trades in names has yours on a slate, priced at forty credits. Forty is insultingly low, and insult is worse than the bounty itself.
neon_city.ev.rumor.4.trace: Buy the name and the seller
neon_city.ev.rumor.4.trace.note: For eighty credits you learn who posted it: Kestrel, testing whether the market still respects your reputation.
neon_city.ev.rumor.4.ignore.note: Within a week your name clears from the slate anyway. Kestrel learns what the Bazaar thinks of his games, and does not enjoy the lesson.
neon_city.ev.journey.1.text: A smuggler at Dock Seven offers you a berth on a boat leaving before dawn. The destination is unlisted, the fare is your whole savings, and the sea is not on any map you trust.
neon_city.ev.journey.1.go.note: You spend six weeks at sea and come back to a city that filed you missing. The horizon was worth it; the return is harder.
neon_city.ev.journey.1.stay.note: The boat leaves at three. You watch the lights go out over the water and are at work by seven, as if nothing at all had happened.
neon_city.ev.journey.2.text: Ash needs a second body for a rooftop run to the far terraces: three nights across the stacks, no nets, and a package that must not get wet.
neon_city.ev.journey.2.go.note: You cross between towers on rusted catwalks and arrive with the package dry. The view from the highest terrace rearranges something in you.
neon_city.ev.journey.2.stay.note: Ash finds another runner and comes back three days later, unhurt and unreadable. You wonder for years what the sky looked like up there.
neon_city.ev.journey.3: The End of the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.journey.3.text: The Spine has a last station that no timetable lists, past the end of the map. The conductor says the train stops there once a month, for anyone willing to be on it.
neon_city.ev.journey.3.go.note: The station is real, half-flooded, and full of people who chose to disappear. You come back with a name you had stopped hoping to find.
neon_city.ev.journey.3.stay.note: You ride past the last stop without looking up from your deck. For months afterward you catch yourself reading the timetable for a line that is not printed.
neon_city.ev.journey.4.text: The Curator opens a link to a sub-net the Directorate sealed decades ago: a crawl through dead servers where the only danger is what you find there.
neon_city.ev.journey.4.go.note: You walk through the archived lower city as it was before the Cold Boot and see your own street as a child. You log out older.
neon_city.ev.journey.4.stay.note: You leave the link dark. The Curator says nothing, but the archive stops sending you birthday reminders.
neon_city.ev.duel.1.text: A rival technician challenges you in front of the Market crowd: same broken limb, same hour, whoever does not crash the patient's firmware wins the crowd's business.
neon_city.ev.duel.1.fight.note: Your patch holds and his reboots mid-test. The crowd remembers your hands, and the Market remembers your name.
neon_city.ev.duel.1.decline.note: He calls you a coward to a crowd that believes him. You keep your record clean and lose a month of stalls.
neon_city.ev.duel.2: The Chase on the Spine - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.duel.2.text: A Freelancer who claims you skipped a contract spots you on the platform and starts running. The train is coming, and the platform ends where the tunnel begins.
neon_city.ev.duel.2.fight.note: You fight on a moving platform and win by knowing where the cameras cannot see. He keeps his life and loses his claim.
neon_city.ev.duel.2.decline.note: You roll down the embankment and escape through the service tunnels. Your knee never fully forgives you, and the story follows you.
neon_city.ev.duel.3: A Knife in the Flood - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.duel.3.text: A debt collector corners you in knee-deep water where no one can see a blade. He gives you the choice that is not a choice: pay tonight, or bleed here.
neon_city.ev.duel.3.fight.note: You end it fast and ugly, and the collector's employer sends someone smarter next time. The Underslum nods when you pass.
neon_city.ev.duel.3.decline.note: You buy a week with a promise you cannot keep. The debt grows interest, and interest in this city has a face.
neon_city.ev.duel.4.text: Mister Pale sets you against another contractor for the same job, head to head, on the terms that the loser is flagged as surplus. Only one of you leaves on payroll.
neon_city.ev.duel.4.fight.note: You undercut the rival and win the contract at a loss. Pale respects the ruthlessness and remembers you as useful, which is better than liked.
neon_city.ev.duel.4.decline.note: You walk out with your margin intact and your standing halved. The rival takes the job, and the blame when it fails.
neon_city.ev.harvest.1.text: The terraces yield more than anyone expected, and less than everyone needs. The wardens say the surplus goes to whoever holds the lease; the growers say it goes to whoever grew it.
neon_city.ev.harvest.1.share.note: You speak up at the wardens' table and lose the argument, but the growers split the crop anyway and count you as one of them.
neon_city.ev.harvest.1.hoard.note: You collect a full share and a full measure of resentment. The next harvest, no one warns you before the wardens audit.
neon_city.ev.harvest.2.text: A derelict tower falls into the flood, offering a season's worth of salvage to whoever reaches it first. The tunnels fill with crews, and crews fill with knives.
neon_city.ev.harvest.2.share.note: You draw lines on a wall and make the crews honor them. The haul is smaller per person and nobody drowns for it.
neon_city.ev.harvest.2.hoard.note: You get the copper and the best boards. Two crews remember, and one of them waits a long time to be even.
neon_city.ev.harvest.3.text: The Gardens recover a cache of pre-Overclock data, uncorrupted and unlicensed. The Directorate wants it, the Wired want it freed, and the Curator wants it kept.
neon_city.ev.harvest.3.share.note: The cache goes out across the mesh and lights up a thousand old debts. The Directorate hunts the leak for a decade.
neon_city.ev.harvest.3.hoard.note: The payment clears the same day. The Curator seals the Gardens to you, and the archived voices stop answering.
neon_city.ev.harvest.4: The Wreck of the Kestrel - Black Bazaar
neon_city.ev.harvest.4.text: A cargo hauler named for the enforcer wrecks in the outer tunnels, spilling sealed crates the Bazaar has already begun to fight over.
neon_city.ev.harvest.4.share: Open the crates in the open
neon_city.ev.harvest.4.share.note: You cut the seals in front of everyone, and the contents are only machine parts. The crowd disperses, disappointed and honest.
neon_city.ev.harvest.4.hoard.note: The crates are worth more than machine parts, and the Bazaar knows you took them. You sell them far away, and never come back to that tunnel.
neon_city.ev.law.1.text: A new Directorate order requires every vendor in the Market to register a retinal scan. The stall next to yours has a forged identity and a family that depends on it.
neon_city.ev.law.1.obey.note: Your scan clears and your neighbor is arrested at dawn. His stall stands empty for a month before a corporate vendor takes it.
neon_city.ev.law.1.defy.note: You buy a bootleg retina file from Silk. The stall survives; Silk now owns a piece of you, and you both know the price.
neon_city.ev.law.2: Curfew on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.law.2.text: The Spine runs a curfew after the Directorate flagged the line as a smuggling route. A passenger beside you has no pass and nowhere to be at this hour.
neon_city.ev.law.2.obey.note: The inspectors take her off at the next stop. You tell yourself it was not your problem, and the phrase wears thin by the time you get home.
neon_city.ev.law.2.defy.note: She makes it through and vanishes into the crowd. The badge is flagged for misuse; you report it stolen and live with the thinness of the lie.
neon_city.ev.law.3.text: The landlord posts an eviction order for every tenant on floors eight to eleven, unregistered. Your floor is on the list, and so is the woman who taught you to read.
neon_city.ev.law.3.obey: Pack and find a new floor
neon_city.ev.law.3.obey.note: You leave before the wardens come and lose furniture you cannot replace. The woman stays to fight and is gone by the end of the month.
neon_city.ev.law.3.defy.note: Forty tenants refuse together and the wardens, for once, back down. The landlord files your name first, and files it twice.
neon_city.ev.law.4.text: The Directorate levies a tax on unlicensed personal archives. The Curator has a cache older than the tax law, and a request: do not let the auditors see it.
neon_city.ev.law.4.obey.note: The auditors seize it and pay you a finder's fee that buys a month. The Curator's voice, when it comes, is very quiet.
neon_city.ev.law.4.defy: Hide it in the flood tunnels
neon_city.ev.law.4.defy.note: You move the cache under the waterline where scans cannot reach. The Curator says only: now you are part of the archive.
neon_city.ev.first_love.1.text: You meet at a noodle stall after midnight: a medic off a double shift, too tired to be guarded, stirring her soup without eating it.
neon_city.ev.first_love.1.woo.note: You walk her through three tunnels and learn her name, her shift, and the name of the brother she is paying for. She asks to see you again.
neon_city.ev.first_love.1.friend: Buy her soup and talk shop
neon_city.ev.first_love.1.friend.note: You talk about triage until the stall closes and part as colleagues. Years later she is the one who answers when you call.
neon_city.ev.first_love.2: The Grower at Harvest - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.first_love.2.text: On the terraces, a grower hands you a tomato she grew from a seed she smuggled up in her boot, and laughs at your face when you bite it.
neon_city.ev.first_love.2.woo.note: She shows you every row and talks until the grow-lights dim. You learn that a person who grows things is hard to lie to.
neon_city.ev.first_love.2.friend.note: You part at the ladder with tomato juice on your hands. She marries a warden next year, and you still remember the taste.
neon_city.ev.first_love.3: The Musician between Stops - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.first_love.3.text: A busker plays on the Spine without a license, and the sound carries between two stations before the inspector walks through. You are standing close enough to warn him.
neon_city.ev.first_love.3.woo.note: He packs up and plays for you alone in the last carriage. You miss your stop on purpose and do not regret it.
neon_city.ev.first_love.3.friend.note: You hear the inspector's whistle behind you as the doors close. The song stays with you for days, and so does the doubt.
neon_city.ev.first_love.4: The Archivist Who Remembers - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.first_love.4.text: The Curator introduces you to a junior archivist, mostly flesh and partly archived, who remembers a childhood that may not have happened.
neon_city.ev.first_love.4.woo.note: She tells you a childhood in the old lower city, archived from a stranger. You decide not to care whose it was, and she notices that you decided.
neon_city.ev.first_love.4.friend.note: You spend the shift sorting dead formats. She calls you a good colleague, and means it, and that is its own kind of door closing.
neon_city.ev.grief.1: The Job That Went Wrong - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.grief.1.text: Your old running partner is pulled out of a flooded tunnel after a job you both refused and he took alone. The crew lays him on the platform and waits for someone who knew him.
neon_city.ev.grief.1.mourn.note: You sit until the pumps come on and the water starts to rise again. You learn his real name, which he never told you while he could.
neon_city.ev.grief.1.carry: Take the next job that night
neon_city.ev.grief.1.carry.note: You work through the grief and finish with clean hands. The crew thinks you are cold, and they are not entirely wrong.
neon_city.ev.grief.2: A Child of the Block - The Stackblocks
neon_city.ev.grief.2.text: The fever takes the child from floor nine. The family cannot afford a wake, so the block holds one in the corridor with borrowed candles.
neon_city.ev.grief.2.mourn.note: You stand in the candlelight and say the child's name when your turn comes. For a week afterward the corridor is gentler with everyone.
neon_city.ev.grief.2.carry.note: You press your last credits into the mother's hand and leave before she can thank you. It is not enough, and she remembers it anyway.
neon_city.ev.grief.3: A Death in the Market - Chrome Market
neon_city.ev.grief.3.text: A ripperdoc you apprenticed beside is found dead over a patient he could not save. The Market says the patient's family paid to make an example.
neon_city.ev.grief.3.mourn: Close his stall for the day
neon_city.ev.grief.3.mourn.note: You pull the shutter and sit in his chair. Someone has to, and no one else comes; the Market does not stop for grief.
neon_city.ev.grief.3.carry.note: You finish his queue and take the beating he was owed. His regulars adopt you, and his enemies file your name beside his.
neon_city.ev.grief.4: An Old Grower Passes - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.grief.4.text: The oldest grower on the terraces dies in her bed among her rows. She leaves no family, only a seed vault with instructions written in a dead language.
neon_city.ev.grief.4.mourn.note: You read the instructions and plant the vault in the spring. The crop that comes up is a variety no one on the terraces has seen in fifty years.
neon_city.ev.grief.4.carry.note: A Spire agronomy lab pays well for the seeds. The terraces lose a library they did not know they had, and the rows come up empty.
neon_city.ev.craft.1.text: A retired lens-maker offers to teach you to grind and implant a custom optic, a craft the Market has almost forgotten under the cheap printed models.
neon_city.ev.craft.1.take.note: You spend months on the bench and learn to see in spectrums the printers cannot touch. Your customers start asking for your work by name.
neon_city.ev.craft.1.refuse.note: You keep the reliable trade and lose the craft. When her bench closes for good, the skill goes with her.
neon_city.ev.craft.2.text: A retired thief shows you the old manual locks under the Spire, the mechanical ones the mesh cannot hack, and offers to teach you the touch.
neon_city.ev.craft.2.take.note: Your fingers learn what firmware never could. On a job years later, a dead mechanical door opens for you while three netrunners argue with the mesh.
neon_city.ev.craft.2.refuse.note: You buy an intrusion deck and trust it. It works until the Spire resets its firmware, and then it works for the Spire.
neon_city.ev.craft.3.text: The Curator teaches you to restore a corrupted archive by hand, byte by byte, matching it against the city's living memory when the checksums are gone.
neon_city.ev.craft.3.take.note: You recover a district's worth of lost names in a single season. Some of the restored files address you by name back.
neon_city.ev.craft.3.refuse.note: You keep your distance from the archives. The Curator marks you as one who will not carry the past, and stops offering.
neon_city.ev.craft.4: Gene Craft on the Terrace - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.craft.4.text: A terrace gene-smith offers to teach you to splice a crop that grows in acid water and poor light, the only agriculture this city has left.
neon_city.ev.craft.4.take.note: Your first strain feeds the terrace through a bad winter. The Directorate, hearing of it, offers to buy the line and does not like your answer.
neon_city.ev.craft.4.refuse.note: You tend the proven crop and watch the smith's new strains feed whole blocks. Your rows survive; hers thrive.
neon_city.ev.secret.1.text: In a dead archive you find proof that the Cold Boot did not just wipe the lower registry: an entire district, its people and their records, was deliberately erased, and one engineer kept a copy.
neon_city.ev.secret.1.open.note: The file goes out on the Wired and the city ripples. The engineer is found dead within the month and the district's name is spoken again.
neon_city.ev.secret.1.leave.note: You hold the copy and check it every night. The engineer's family never learns why the Directorate stopped auditing them.
neon_city.ev.secret.2.text: You discover your quiet neighbor is a Ghost, unindexed, living off a dead man's medical access and a borrowed shift card. She has been here for years.
neon_city.ev.secret.2.open.note: The Directorate pays a bounty and re-registers her as anonymous remains. The room next door is emptied by a team that does not speak.
neon_city.ev.secret.2.leave.note: You forge her a new shift card and never ask why she cried. She starts leaving food at your door, always when you are out.
neon_city.ev.secret.3.text: You catch Silk without the mask and recognize the face: your mother's oldest friend, who supposedly died in the Copper Uprising forty years ago.
neon_city.ev.secret.3.open.note: The buyer is Kestrel, and the price is good. Silk never confirms you did it, and somehow that is worse than being confronted.
neon_city.ev.secret.3.leave.note: Silk knows that you know, and treats you better for it. You never tell Mama Sol that her friend is alive and wearing other people's faces.
neon_city.ev.secret.4.text: Behind a locked ward you find the clinic harvesting organs from unregistered patients, the ones nobody would miss. Doc Halsey's signature is on the requisitions.
neon_city.ev.secret.4.open.note: He does not deny it. He says it is the only reason the ward still runs, and asks what you would have done with the bodies. You have no answer.
neon_city.ev.secret.4.leave.note: You lock the door and never mention it. Every transplant you see afterward makes you check the donor's file.
neon_city.ev.drought.1.text: The condensation lines narrow and the terrace rations cut by half. The greens wilt in rows, and the wardens say the cut is temporary, as they said last year.
neon_city.ev.drought.1.ration.note: Everyone loses a little and the terrace survives together. The harvest is thin, and no row is empty, which is its own victory.
neon_city.ev.drought.1.take: Trick the meters for your rows
neon_city.ev.drought.1.take.note: Your rows flourish while others fail. The wardens trace the flow within a month, and the growers trace it faster.
neon_city.ev.drought.2.text: The pumps die and the floodwater drops, taking the drinking supply with it. Clean water begins selling by the cup, then by the sip.
neon_city.ev.drought.2.ration.note: You stand watch over the last clean water and set the ration by hand. No one dies of thirst, and no one thanks you for the rules.
neon_city.ev.drought.2.take.note: You secure a private supply and sell the surplus high. The credits are real, and so is the knife that is coming in the dark.
neon_city.ev.drought.3.text: The coolant supply dries up during a heat wave. The chrome in the city runs hot, and the clinics are taking in burns that were not there last week.
neon_city.ev.drought.3.ration.note: You give your share to the patients with fevered implants. Your own arm runs hot for a week, and you learn the exact temperature of patience.
neon_city.ev.drought.3.take.note: You corner a stall's worth of coolant and earn a killing. Two people burn out their nervous systems, and the Market notes who sold.
neon_city.ev.drought.4.text: The Directorate throttles the free mesh and rations bandwidth. The archives begin to degrade file by file, and the Curator cannot save all of them.
neon_city.ev.drought.4.ration.note: You save the pre-Overclock archive and lose a decade of ordinary records. The Curator calls the trade correct and does not sound certain.
neon_city.ev.drought.4.take.note: You broker a stolen allotment at a premium. The Gardens keep more rooms alive, and the Directorate opens a file with your handle on it.
neon_city.ev.gift.1.text: A courier leaves a sealed chip at your door: encrypted, addressed to a handle you stopped using years ago, postmarked from a district that no longer exists.
neon_city.ev.gift.1.accept.note: It is a full ledger of debts owed to you, compiled by someone who has watched you a long time. The list is longer than your memory, and it is genuine.
neon_city.ev.gift.1.suspect.note: You drop the chip down a drain and sleep badly for a week. Years later the same courier delivers another, and you finally open that one.
neon_city.ev.gift.2: Breakfast at the Door - The Stackblocks
neon_city.ev.gift.2.text: For the third morning running, a hot bun and a cup of real tea wait at your door, still warm, no note, no name, no one in the corridor.
neon_city.ev.gift.2.accept.note: The next morning the thank-you is gone and breakfast is doubled. You never learn which of your neighbors it is, and it becomes a quiet game.
neon_city.ev.gift.2.suspect.note: You catch the person at the door: the child from floor nine you once carried water for. She runs before you can say anything.
neon_city.ev.gift.3: A Gift from Above - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.gift.3.text: Mister Pale sends you a case of premium components, no invoice, with an unsigned note that says only: for services anticipated.
neon_city.ev.gift.3.accept.note: The parts are the best you have ever owned. Three weeks later Pale calls in the anticipated service, and the debt is suddenly very specific.
neon_city.ev.gift.3.suspect.note: You send it back with a note of your own. Pale does not punish you, and does not offer again, and that absence is its own punishment.
neon_city.ev.gift.4.text: The Curator restores a fragment of your own childhood you had lost to a cheap implant wipe: a kitchen, a song, a voice you had stopped being able to hear.
neon_city.ev.gift.4.accept.note: The voice is Mama Sol's, younger, singing something you had forgotten. You sit in the racks a long time afterward, and go home and call her.
neon_city.ev.gift.4.suspect.note: You ask the Curator to keep it sealed. It stays in the archive under your name, and you visit the shelf without ever asking for it.
neon_city.ev.war.1.text: Two Freelancer crews go to war over the Spine, and the line becomes a moving battlefield. The Directorate closes the stations and leaves the passengers to whoever wins.
neon_city.ev.war.1.serve: Volunteer as a medic on the line
neon_city.ev.war.1.serve.note: You patch wounds between stops for three days and see things that do not leave you. Both crews remember your hands, and none of them shoot at you.
neon_city.ev.war.1.hide.note: You walk the long way for a month and lose the work the line carried. The war ends; the two crews are smaller, and the stations reopen.
neon_city.ev.war.2.text: The Couriers and the Ghosts fight for the flood tunnels. The Couriers move goods; the Ghosts move nothing and want the tunnels empty. You live on the contested stretch.
neon_city.ev.war.2.serve.note: You guide three runs past the Ghosts and earn the Couriers' protection. The Ghosts mark you, and their mark does not wash off.
neon_city.ev.war.2.hide.note: You live on stored protein until the shooting stops. The Couriers win the tunnels and both sides remember who stayed neutral, in different ways.
neon_city.ev.war.3.text: Two directorates inside the Spire are quietly at war, and both want your name attached to their side. The loser of this war is not likely to leave the tower.
neon_city.ev.war.3.serve: Pick the side that pays first
neon_city.ev.war.3.serve.note: You contract to the directorate with the deeper accounts. When they win, you are useful; when their rival falls, you are complicit, and that is survivable.
neon_city.ev.war.3.hide.note: You play both sides for months and come out with money and no allies. The moment the war ends, both sides discover they were played.
neon_city.ev.war.4.text: Two terraces sabotage each other's condensation lines over a disputed ration, and the conflict is heading for knives on the catwalks.
neon_city.ev.war.4.serve.note: You spend two weeks walking between roofs and draw a line both sides hate equally. It holds, mostly, and the harvest comes in.
neon_city.ev.war.4.hide.note: You leave before the first sabotage and watch from a distance. The war takes one life and two seasons, and your new rows are undisturbed.
neon_city.ev.famine.1.text: The synth-protein vats fail, and the Underslum's cheapest food disappears overnight. The stalls close, and the lines at the remaining ones stretch for blocks.
neon_city.ev.famine.1.share.note: You feed your tunnel until your own shelf is bare. Your neighbors survive the worst month, and your name becomes safe in places it was not.
neon_city.ev.famine.1.close: Lock your door and eat alone
neon_city.ev.famine.1.close.note: You ration in silence and listen to the arguments in the corridor. You come through the shortage heavier than most, and it costs what it costs.
neon_city.ev.famine.2.text: The building committee meets to decide whether to ration the communal kitchen by floor, by family, or by who is willing to work the line.
neon_city.ev.famine.2.share.note: You get the ration tied to children and the sick. The single workers resent it and understand it. The block comes through without a death.
neon_city.ev.famine.2.close.note: You quietly move supplies to your own level. The lower floors go hungry for a week, and the elevator stops answering your calls.
neon_city.ev.famine.3.text: A blight takes every terrace at once. The farms that feed the lower city fail in a single season, and the wardens ask the growers to destroy the sick crop to save the seed.
neon_city.ev.famine.3.share: Burn the crop, save the seed
neon_city.ev.famine.3.share.note: You burn your rows with your own hands and keep the vault for spring. The winter is lean, and the terrace returns, which the other choice would not have.
neon_city.ev.famine.3.close.note: You keep a private crop alive and sell it high through the winter. The terrace learns who prospered, and the next planting excludes you.
neon_city.ev.famine.4.text: The Bazaar's food stalls ration by name, and the names are written by the stallholders. You are offered a place on the list, at the price of reporting who else should be cut.
neon_city.ev.famine.4.share.note: You eat less and keep your hands clean. The list is written by someone else and includes three people you know, and it is shorter for your refusal.
neon_city.ev.famine.4.close: Take the place and write the list
neon_city.ev.famine.4.close.note: You eat, and you write the list, and you are careful to exclude the ones you owe. It is a small mercy in a structure that has none.
neon_city.ev.tradition.1: The Light for the Missing - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.tradition.1.text: The Underslum keeps an old custom: on the shortest night, every household leaves one light on for the missing, whether they are gone to the tunnels, the Spire, or the sea.
neon_city.ev.tradition.1.keep.note: You burn your last good bulb all night, and someone across the water does the same, and you sit together in the dark without speaking.
neon_city.ev.tradition.1.break.note: You sleep in the dark to save current. In the morning you cannot stop thinking about the light you did not leave.
neon_city.ev.tradition.2.text: The block's oldest custom: when the elevator breaks, the whole building repairs it together, floor by floor, and whoever cannot lift brings food and song.
neon_city.ev.tradition.2.keep.note: You spend the day hauling cable and learning the names of five floors. The elevator works for a month before it breaks again, and the festival comes with it.
neon_city.ev.tradition.2.break.note: The repair is faster and you skip the day. The car works longer, and no one on the stairs greets you for a while.
neon_city.ev.tradition.3.text: The Curator performs an archive rite each solstice: the names of the erased are read aloud into the racks, so that the deletion is at least witnessed.
neon_city.ev.tradition.3.keep.note: You read four names you never knew and hear them echo in the server hum. It is not resurrection, but it is not silence either.
neon_city.ev.tradition.3.break.note: You work through the solstice and let the rite pass. That night the archive logs an unassigned playback, and the Curator does not mention it.
neon_city.ev.tradition.4.text: The Directorate holds its annual renewal ceremony, where employees surrender last year's identity chip and receive a new one, freshly printed, with new permissions.
neon_city.ev.tradition.4.keep.note: The new permissions are better and your old history is gone. You spend months discovering which of your own memories no longer have a file.
neon_city.ev.tradition.4.break.note: You take the new chip and keep the old one in your boot. The old one still opens three doors the Directorate forgot, and one of them matters later.
neon_city.ev.legacy.1: What You Leave the Tunnel Kids - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.legacy.1.text: The tunnel kids watch you work and copy your hands. They have no school and no papers, and whatever they learn, they will learn from someone. Tonight, that someone is you.
neon_city.ev.legacy.1.write.note: You spend your evenings showing them locks and splices and the tricks that keep a runner alive. Years later, three of them carry your method.
neon_city.ev.legacy.1.silent.note: You work alone and the kids drift to worse teachers. One of them takes a job that kills him, and you hear about it in a stall three tunnels away.
neon_city.ev.legacy.2.text: The Curator offers to archive your life: every document, every log, every recorded word. It would outlast you, and it would not be private.
neon_city.ev.legacy.2.write.note: The Curator files your life among the district records. Strangers read it for years; some of them write back to the shelves, and the Curator reads you their replies.
neon_city.ev.legacy.2.silent.note: You leave no archive and no trail. After you, the only proof you lived is what people remember, and memory in this city is thin.
neon_city.ev.legacy.3.text: The terrace offers you a share in the long planting: a vault of seeds kept for whoever comes after the current drought, on the condition that you tend it for years.
neon_city.ev.legacy.3.write.note: You tend the vault through two bad seasons and never eat from it. The terrace that inherits it will never know your name, and it will eat.
neon_city.ev.legacy.3.silent.note: You keep your hands free and your rows your own. The vault passes to a family with more patience, and you watch it from across the terrace.
neon_city.ev.legacy.4: The Truth for Mio - The Stackblocks
neon_city.ev.legacy.4.text: Little Mio comes home for one night and asks, for the first time, what really happened the year the district was erased, and why the family never talks about it.
neon_city.ev.legacy.4.write.note: You tell her about the Cold Boot and the copy your family kept. She leaves the Spire academy within the year, and you are not sure whether to be proud.
neon_city.ev.legacy.4.silent.note: You tell her it was a fire and she believes you, because she wants to. She stays in the towers, and the truth stays with you, and it is heavy.
neon_city.ev.temptation.1.text: A dealer offers a combat chip that does not make you stronger, only fearless. The first dose is free. The second will cost more than you have.
neon_city.ev.temptation.1.resist.note: You leave the stall with your fear intact, which is the only reason you keep checking your corners. You watch the chip spread among the less careful.
neon_city.ev.temptation.1.yield.note: The fear goes and does not come back on schedule. Two runs later you take a wound you should have seen, and the dealer's second price is everything.
neon_city.ev.temptation.2: A Signature for a Cut - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.temptation.2.text: A rival offers to let you sign work you did not do, for a share of the credit. The work is good, the credit is real, and no one but the two of you will ever know.
neon_city.ev.temptation.2.resist.note: You give up the credit and keep your name honest. The rival resents you for the refusal, which tells you the refusal was right.
neon_city.ev.temptation.2.yield.note: The credit opens doors for a season. Then the rival's real client discovers the deception, and both your names fall together.
neon_city.ev.temptation.3.text: A vendor offers to install a premium deck upgrade for free, today only, no questions. The firmware hash does not match anything published, and he shrugs when you mention it.
neon_city.ev.temptation.3.resist.note: You buy the licensed part instead and skip a month of noodles. Six weeks later the free upgrade bricks seventeen decks across the market.
neon_city.ev.temptation.3.yield.note: The upgrade is fast and smooth and logs everything you do. When the vendor's employer calls in the debt, your entire history is already in their hands.
neon_city.ev.temptation.4: A New Name on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.temptation.4.text: A stranger on the Spine offers you a complete identity: clean papers, distant district, a life with no debts attached, for a fraction of what it would cost to earn one.
neon_city.ev.temptation.4.resist.note: You ride to your stop as yourself, debts and all. The stranger gets off two stations later with the papers still in his coat.
neon_city.ev.temptation.4.yield.note: For one month the new name is a kind of rest. Then the identity's original owner surfaces, and the Directorate follows, and the debt is now a crime.
neon_city.ev.rescue.1.text: A stall scaffold gives way and a vendor is pinned beneath, conscious and bleeding, while the crowd around you takes out their decks to record instead of lift.
neon_city.ev.rescue.1.help.note: You and two strangers get the weight off him before the clinic crew arrives. Your back twinges for a month, and he never forgets your face.
neon_city.ev.rescue.1.pass: Call the clinic and step back
neon_city.ev.rescue.1.pass.note: The clinic crew takes nine minutes to arrive. The vendor lives and loses the use of a hand, and the crowd's recordings are the only witnesses.
neon_city.ev.rescue.2: A Child in the Flood - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.rescue.2.text: A child goes under the floodwater between two tunnels and does not come up. The current is fast, the water is filthy, and no one else has moved.
neon_city.ev.rescue.2.help.note: You pull her out coughing and shaking. Her mother gives you everything she has, and you take none of it, and the tunnel remembers you for years.
neon_city.ev.rescue.2.pass.note: The crews find her downstream, alive but changed. You tell yourself you did the sensible thing, and the floodwater in your dreams disagrees.
neon_city.ev.rescue.3.text: A security lockdown seals a junior employee inside a failing server room during a Directorate purge. Her calls for help route to you, because your handle is the only one she knows.
neon_city.ev.rescue.3.help.note: You spoof a maintenance override and get her out before the room seals for good. The Directorate never identifies the override, and she owes you a life.
neon_city.ev.rescue.3.pass.note: Security arrives, logs the incident, and leaves her inside until the purge is complete. Her calls stop at 3:14, and the file closes as a systems fault.
neon_city.ev.rescue.4.text: A catwalk line snaps in the wind and a worker is left hanging by one harness strap above the terrace, far enough to break everything if she falls.
neon_city.ev.rescue.4.help.note: You cross the swaying gap and haul her back by the strap. The terrace gives you a row of your own, which is their way of saying it and never saying it.
neon_city.ev.rescue.4.pass.note: The rig takes twenty minutes and she holds on. She walks away, and stops speaking to you, and you both know exactly why.
neon_city.ev.bargain.1: Hot Implants in the Bazaar - Black Bazaar
neon_city.ev.bargain.1.text: A dealer in the Bazaar offers a set of top-grade implants at a tenth of market price, still warm, still logged in to someone else's biometrics.
neon_city.ev.bargain.1.deal.note: The implants work flawlessly for a year. Then their original owner's employer traces the biometric log, and the flaw becomes an address with your door on it.
neon_city.ev.bargain.1.walk.note: You buy nothing and keep your name off the log. The next buyer is caught within a week, and you hear about it over noodles and feel nothing but luck.
neon_city.ev.bargain.2: The Contract with a Clause - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.bargain.2.text: Mister Pale offers a contract with a payout that would clear every debt you have, and a liability clause buried on page nine that you are not permitted to copy.
neon_city.ev.bargain.2.deal.note: The money clears your debts within the month. The clause surfaces two years later, and by then it owns the assets you bought with the payout.
neon_city.ev.bargain.2.walk.note: You insist on a night to read it, and Pale, amused, agrees. In the morning you decline, and he respects you and never offers so good a number again.
neon_city.ev.bargain.3: Credit at the Clinic - Clinic Vault
neon_city.ev.bargain.3.text: Doc Halsey offers to patch you up on credit: the operation now, the payment whenever you can. He does not say what happens if you cannot.
neon_city.ev.bargain.3.deal.note: You wake repaired and in debt to Halsey. He never presses you for it, which somehow makes the number larger every month.
neon_city.ev.bargain.3.walk.note: You limp for six months and keep your account clean. Halsey shakes his head, patches you anyway at cost, and calls it a professional courtesy.
neon_city.ev.bargain.4: A Favor for the Archive - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.bargain.4.text: The Curator offers a piece of knowledge you have wanted for years, in exchange for a single favor to be named later: no terms, no limit, no refusal.
neon_city.ev.bargain.4.deal.note: You learn what you wanted and spend years waiting for the favor to be called. When it comes, it is smaller than you feared and stranger than you imagined.
neon_city.ev.bargain.4.walk.note: You decline the knowledge and keep your freedom. The Curator marks you as careful, which closes some doors and opens others.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.1: The Storm in the Tunnels - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.storm_night.1.text: The storm above pushes the floodwater into the Underslum, and your flooded neighbor pounds on your door with her children behind her, asking for higher ground.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.1.shelter.note: You give them your dry room and sleep on the stairs. The water rises to your ankles and stops, and the children sleep through the worst of it.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.1.self.note: You keep your room dry and listen to her pound until she finds another door. She and the children survive, and she does not look at you again.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.2.text: The wind tears the facade panels off your block and exposes the whole floor to the rain. The tenants gather in the corridor to decide which rooms to shore up with what is left.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.2.shelter.note: Your room floods so that the nursery on floor seven stays dry. The block remembers, and the water damage is only money.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.2.self.note: Your room stays dry and the corridor does not. The nursery moves to a wet floor for a month, and nobody says anything to you about it, which is worse.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.3.text: The storm shreds the terrace covers and the beds are exposed to acid rain. You have one working tarp and time to cover either your rows or the communal seed beds.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.3.shelter.note: Your rows die and the seed beds live. The terrace replants from the vault in spring, and your row is replanted first, by other hands.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.3.self.note: Your harvest survives and the seed beds are scalded. The terrace loses a season, and you eat while it does, and the taste does not improve.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.4.text: The storm cuts the power and the Spine stops between stations with a carriage full of strangers and no signal. The air runs out in six hours unless someone walks the tunnel.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.4.shelter.note: You and two others walk the flooded service line to the next station and bring back a crew. The carriage breathes again, and the tunnel costs you a shoe and some hearing.
neon_city.ev.storm_night.4.self: Wait for the power to return
neon_city.ev.storm_night.4.self.note: You conserve air and calm the carriage as best you can. The power returns with an hour to spare, and one passenger still does not wake up.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.1.text: A Spire academy offers you a place on a sponsored course: four years of training, a real credential, and a contract that owns the next decade of your work.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.1.study.note: You learn more in four years than the lower city could teach in twenty. You also sign away the decade, and you spend it being grateful and bitter at once.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.1.play.note: You keep your independence and learn on the job. The credential goes to someone slower, who spends the decade being promoted over you.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.2: Tutoring in the Racks - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.scholarship.2.text: The Curator offers to teach you the deep archive: indexing, decryption, and the memory arts no academy still holds a syllabus for.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.2.study.note: You learn to read a city the way the Curator does, in layers and omissions. The Directorate has no rank for your skill, which is exactly why it is useful.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.2.play.note: You pick up the practical indexing and stop. The Curator closes the deeper files and does not invite you back to the shelves.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.3.text: The lens-maker who taught you once is dying and wants one full apprenticeship before her bench closes. It would take two years and pay nothing.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.3.study.note: You spend two unpaid years learning a craft that is already dying. You also inherit her tools, her clients, and the only unbroken tradition on the Market.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.3.play.note: You earn steadily for two years and learn nothing you could not have bought. The bench closes with the old woman, and the tools go to a museum in the Spire.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.4: Lessons in the Tunnel - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.scholarship.4.text: A self-taught engineer who has never been inside a school offers to teach you what the academies cannot: how the Underslum actually keeps working.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.4.study.note: You learn to fix a pump with a dead man's parts and keep a whole tunnel breathing. It is not a credential, and it saves your life more than once.
neon_city.ev.scholarship.4.play.note: You apply the proper method and the pump fails anyway. The engineer fixes it in ten minutes and does not offer to teach you again.
neon_city.ev.honor.1: The Tunnel Named for You - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.honor.1.text: The Underslum proposes to name a flooded tunnel after you, in spray paint and in the water, for something you did that you thought no one saw.
neon_city.ev.honor.1.accept.note: The name goes up on the tunnel wall and stays there through three floods. Runners you never met use it as a landmark and as a warning.
neon_city.ev.honor.1.decline: Ask them to name it for the dead
neon_city.ev.honor.1.decline.note: The tunnel takes the name of the partner you lost, which you never said aloud. The Underslum agrees without asking why, because it already knew.
neon_city.ev.honor.2.text: A director offers you a service medal and a bonus for a job that, in truth, you did for your own reasons and would do again for free.
neon_city.ev.honor.2.accept.note: You pin the medal on once and never again. The bonus pays a debt; the medal makes you visible to people who keep lists of the decorated.
neon_city.ev.honor.2.decline.note: You take the bonus and skip the stage. The director is puzzled and a little offended, and the people who keep lists never hear your name.
neon_city.ev.honor.3: A Row with Your Name - Roof Farms
neon_city.ev.honor.3.text: The terrace offers to name a row after you at the next planting: a stripe of green with your name on the water marker, for as long as the terrace stands.
neon_city.ev.honor.3.accept.note: Your name waters a row you will never eat from. Children you never met pick from it and mispronounce you, and that is exactly the point.
neon_city.ev.honor.3.decline.note: The row is planted unnamed and grows just as well. The growers think you modest and are disappointed; you preferred it this way.
neon_city.ev.honor.4.text: The Market's old benches offer you a maker's mark: a stamp on your work that tells every buyer it was done by a hand the Market trusts.
neon_city.ev.honor.4.accept.note: Your work prices higher from the first day. You also answer for everything bearing your mark, including two jobs you did not do and cannot disown.
neon_city.ev.honor.4.decline.note: You keep your prices low and your name clean. A buyer resells your work under another maker's mark and earns ten times what you did.
neon_city.ev.lost.1: Lost in the Blackout - The Stackblocks
neon_city.ev.lost.1.text: A blackout takes the stairs and the signage with it, and you cannot find your own floor. The stairwell is full of neighbors doing the same, counting landings in the dark.
neon_city.ev.lost.1.call.note: A voice two landings up answers by number and walks you down. You never see the face, and the next blackout you are the one calling out.
neon_city.ev.lost.1.wait: Sit and wait for the lights
neon_city.ev.lost.1.wait.note: You sit on the stairs for four hours and count the building's sounds. You find your floor when the power returns, and you never quite forget the dark.
neon_city.ev.lost.2: Lost under the Waterline - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.lost.2.text: Your deck dies in a dead zone and you realize you have been walking the same three tunnels for an hour. The water is rising, and no one answers a shout.
neon_city.ev.lost.2.call.note: A scavenger hears you and leads you out for a fee. She could have taken everything; the fact that she did not is the whole of your luck that night.
neon_city.ev.lost.2.wait: Sit above the water and wait
neon_city.ev.lost.2.wait.note: You climb a maintenance ledge and wait out the tide. It takes six hours and you come out with a fever and a new respect for the tunnels.
neon_city.ev.lost.3: Lost on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.lost.3.text: You fall asleep on the Spine and wake at the far end of the line, past your station and past the last one on the map, in a carriage that is suddenly almost empty.
neon_city.ev.lost.3.call.note: The conductor walks you to a return train and does not charge you. She says people get lost on this line more than anyone reports.
neon_city.ev.lost.3.wait: Ride it back on your own
neon_city.ev.lost.3.wait.note: You ride the loop for three hours until the line resets. You see three stations that are not on any timetable, and tell no one.
neon_city.ev.lost.4: Lost in the Tower - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.lost.4.text: A service elevator takes you to a floor with no directory, no windows, and identical corridors that do not appear in the building plans. Your badge does not open anything here.
neon_city.ev.lost.4.call.note: Security retrieves you in twenty minutes and asks you three times how you got there. Your badge is reissued with fewer permissions, and no one explains.
neon_city.ev.lost.4.wait: Walk until you find a stairwell
neon_city.ev.lost.4.wait.note: You find a stairwell, and a door marked with a district name the Directorate erased. You leave the way you came and never find the floor again.
neon_city.ev.dream.1.text: The memory shard you bought has begun bleeding into your sleep: a kitchen you never had, a parent you never met, a name you wake up almost saying.
neon_city.ev.dream.1.follow.note: You live a whole borrowed summer in three nights. It leaves you gentler and stranger, and you return the shard before it can take more.
neon_city.ev.dream.1.wake.note: You set alarms to break the dream and lose the rest of the week to exhaustion. The kitchen fades, and you miss it, which is the troubling part.
neon_city.ev.dream.2.text: You dream the same dream three nights running: the waterline rising past every floor, the Spire's lights going out from the bottom up, and no one in the city able to swim.
neon_city.ev.dream.2.follow.note: You log every detail, and the fourth night the dream changes: a door in the water, and on the other side, a dry street from before the flood. You wake calm.
neon_city.ev.dream.2.wake.note: The dream stops visiting and the fear stays. You keep a light burning and your current bill climbs, and the tunnels feel colder than they used to.
neon_city.ev.dream.3: The Roof of the Tower - Corporate Spire
neon_city.ev.dream.3.text: You dream of standing on the Spire's roof with the rain below you, warm air around you, and the whole city laid out like a board you could move pieces on.
neon_city.ev.dream.3.follow.note: You start taking the stairs instead of the elevator, a floor a week, toward something. You never reach the roof, and you are healthier than you have been in years.
neon_city.ev.dream.3.wake.note: You dismiss the dream and stay in the lower city. The ambition does not return, which is a relief, and occasionally a regret.
neon_city.ev.dream.4: The Name in the Static - The Underslum
neon_city.ev.dream.4.text: Between stations in the dead zone, a voice in the static repeats a name you do not recognize and asks, over and over, whether you remember it. You are beginning to.
neon_city.ev.dream.4.follow.note: You say yes, though it is not true yet. The static quiets, and you spend a season tracking the name to an erased district and to a family still waiting.
neon_city.ev.dream.4.wake.note: You kill the receiver and the voice stops. The name surfaces in your dreams for months and you never look it up, and that is a choice you keep making.
neon_city.ev.bet.1.text: In a flooded pit beneath the Bazaar, two chrome fighters go at it while the crowd wagers. A bookmaker with a slate offers you odds on the smaller one, and he is very small indeed.
neon_city.ev.bet.1.match.note: The small one wins on a lucky choke and pays out four to one. The bookmaker pays you slowly, staring, and you cash out before the crowd turns mean.
neon_city.ev.bet.1.fold.note: You watch the small one lose as expected and keep your money. The pit takes a tooth from him and gives you nothing but the memory of the sound.
neon_city.ev.bet.2: The Count on the Line - Transit Spine
neon_city.ev.bet.2.text: Riders wager on how many stations the Spine will skip tonight, and a regular with a formula offers to sell you his numbers for a cut of your winnings.
neon_city.ev.bet.2.match.note: His formula is right twice and wrong once; you come out ahead and he takes his cut. The third time, you lose and learn the formula is his, not the line's.
neon_city.ev.bet.2.fold.note: You watch the night's counts and keep your credits. By the end of the month you have a formula of your own, and no one to sell it to.
neon_city.ev.bet.3.text: Two netrunners race the same Spire node on a public feed, and the Market wagers on the winner. One of them offers you a stake in her run for half the take.
neon_city.ev.bet.3.match.note: She wins by a hair, and the take is real. She also leaves a trail that ends at your name, which the Spire discovers a month later.
neon_city.ev.bet.3.fold.note: You bet nothing and enjoy the race. The loser is flagged and disappears; the winner starts avoiding you, which tells you the outcome you missed.
neon_city.ev.bet.4.text: In a break room, staff run a pool on which of two directorates will fold first in the merger. It is technically insider trading, and everyone from the mail desk up is in.
neon_city.ev.bet.4.match.note: Your pick folds second and you lose the pool. The winner is a mail clerk who knows more about the merger than any analyst, and puts his winnings into silence.
neon_city.ev.bet.4.fold.note: You keep your credits and your record clean. When audit season comes, the pool is discovered, and everyone in it is quietly demoted except you.
neon_city.ev.hermit.1.text: On a decommissioned floor of the Spire lives a man who unplugged decades ago: no mesh, no chrome, no record. He trades hand-written notes with the city through a mail slot and has never been seen leaving.
neon_city.ev.hermit.1.learn.note: He talks for hours about a city with fewer walls. You leave with a paper map of the old districts and a habit of turning your deck off at night.
neon_city.ev.hermit.1.mock.note: He does not argue; he closes the slot and does not answer for a year. The floor goes quiet, and the quiet follows you home.
neon_city.ev.hermit.2.text: An old woman on the top floor keeps a library of paper books and refuses every implant the clinic offers. She reads by window light and calls the mesh a bad habit the whole city shares.
neon_city.ev.hermit.2.learn.note: She lends you a water-damaged novel and makes you promise to return it. You read it slowly and come back, and the visits become a year of Thursdays.
neon_city.ev.hermit.2.mock.note: She closes the door and keeps her books. Later you find her floor sealed and her library gone to a recycler, and you are one of the reasons no one saved it.
neon_city.ev.hermit.3.text: Deep in the tunnels lives a runner who cut every receiver out of his own head years ago, on purpose. He moves through the mesh's blind spots like a man walking through a wall.
neon_city.ev.hermit.3.learn.note: He teaches you to read a room without a feed: to hear a camera and a footstep and a lie. You never trust a deck over your own eyes again.
neon_city.ev.hermit.3.mock.note: He shrugs, which from him is a speech. He is not the one who gets caught in the next net sweep, and you are not the one who warned him.
neon_city.ev.hermit.4: The Archivist of the Dead Rack - Data Gardens
neon_city.ev.hermit.4.text: In a dead server rack lives an archivist who long ago stopped speaking to people and now speaks only to the files, reading them aloud to keep them from decaying into silence.
neon_city.ev.hermit.4.learn.note: You take a turn reading a district's census aloud and feel the room change. The files stop degrading for a month, and the archivist calls that proof enough.
neon_city.ev.hermit.4.mock: Tell him it is just noise
neon_city.ev.hermit.4.mock.note: He stops mid-sentence and lets the rack go quiet. A week of files decay in that silence, and the Curator never learns who was standing there.
neon_city.ev.quiet.text: For one night the acid thins and the rain comes down almost clean. The city stands still and listens to water that does not hiss.
